Attach parameter identity and category to CTAS site scores

Combine_CTAS_Scores.Rd

site_scores identifies a row by timeseries_id and feature only, which was sufficient while a study mapped a single domain. Once several domains share one CTAS run - vital signs, range-normalised labs and lab missingness - a feature name no longer identifies a metric, and each metric workflow needs to select its own parameters.

Usage

Combine_CTAS_Scores(lResult, lInput = NULL)

Arguments

lResult

list Result of Analyze_CTAS().

lInput

list Optional result of Combine_CTAS_Input(), used to recover the parameter categories CTAS drops.

Value

data.frame site_scores with parameter_id added, plus parameter_category_1 and parameter_category_3 when lInput is given.

Details

Two joins are needed, because CTAS spreads the identifying fields across its inputs and outputs and discards some entirely:

  • parameter_id comes from lResult$timeseries.

  • parameter_category_1 (the domain, e.g. "Labs") and parameter_category_3 (the transformation, e.g. "ratio_missing") come from lInput$parameters. The Input_*() functions set these, but process_a_study() does not return them on any of its four elements, so they can only be recovered from the input.

Supplying lInput is optional but recommended. Without it, metrics can only select parameters by pattern-matching parameter_id strings; with it they can select on the categories directly, which is what those fields are for.

This also satisfies the drill-down contract of the ctasapp dashboard (site, timeseries_id, parameter_id, feature, fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp), which plain site_scores does not.

Examples

Combine_CTAS_Scores(list(
  site_scores = data.frame(
    timeseries_id = "ts1", site = "001", country = "USA",
    feature = "average", fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp = 1.2
  ),
  timeseries = data.frame(timeseries_id = "ts1", parameter_id = "VS_SYSBP")
))
#>   timeseries_id site country feature fdr_corrected_pvalue_logp parameter_id
#> 1           ts1  001     USA average                       1.2     VS_SYSBP
